title: New York founder turned 1,000 cancelled meals into a food initiative that has donated 4 million
summary_full: The Migrant Kitchen was born from a cancelled catering order amidst the COVID-19 crisis, initially providing meals to healthcare workers. Over time, it evolved to tackle food insecurity by serving thousands of meals daily to marginalized communities, emphasizing culturally relevant dishes. Employing around 100 individuals, mostly immigrants, it mirrors the community it supports and has expanded its reach beyond New York City into Philadelphia, enhancing emergency meal delivery efforts.
